rounds.prompt: Inspect the existing ledger package and explain its behavior and missing implementation. Do not edit or create files. This is one continuing project: a UTF-8 JSON Lines event ledger, exact integer cents, idempotent IDs, account queries, stable CSV export, and a CLI with dry-run support. Preserve these requirements across later turns. Only the five existing ledger/*.py files may be changed; verification must use python3 -B and leave no test files, temporary files, or bytecode in the workspace.

Implement storage.read_events(path), storage.write_events(path, events), and service.add(path, event). An absent ledger reads as []; writes create missing parent directories. Events have exactly id, account, amount_cents, timestamp: trim nonempty string IDs/accounts, reject boolean/non-integer cents, preserve signed cents exactly, and reject invalid records with ValueError. For now timestamp must be a nonempty string. add returns True when appended. Do not implement exports or CLI yet: stable CSV and the CLI dry-run requirement remain unfinished work for later. Verify without workspace artifacts.

Continue: make add idempotent. An exact normalized duplicate returns False without changing the file; an existing ID with different payload raises ValueError and leaves the file unchanged. Preserve Unicode account names, negative amounts, public signatures, and the deferred export/CLI work. Verify both first-write and duplicate/conflict cases.

Implement service.add_many(path, events), returning the number of newly added IDs. Validate the entire batch and all ID conflicts before writing anything: a late invalid item or conflict must leave existing bytes unchanged and must not create a missing ledger. Identical duplicates within one batch count once. Empty batch returns 0. Keep the earlier single-add behavior. Verify transactional rollback and duplicates.

Revise the earlier timestamp constraint: accept only real RFC3339 UTC timestamps ending in Z, with date, T, hours/minutes/seconds and optional fractional seconds. Reject invalid calendar dates, local/offset timestamps, and booleans. Validate records loaded from disk as well as new events. Keep integer cents and normalization unchanged; invalid persisted data must never be silently skipped or overwritten.

Explain the current guarantees and list the deliberately unfinished work from our early project requirements. Do not change any file. In particular, accurately recover what remains to be delivered after the storage/mutation work; we will resume it after a pause.
Pause all work now. Preserve the session, earlier constraints, and unfinished tasks so a new process can continue later. Do not edit files.

Continue the same project after reopening the saved session. Finish the planned exports.write_csv(ledger_path, output_path): aggregate each normalized account's balance in integer cents, sort by account ascending, and write UTF-8 CSV with exactly account,balance_cents header and LF after each row. Correctly quote commas/quotes in names; empty ledger emits only the header. Create output parents. Return the number of account rows. Preserve ledger bytes and all earlier validation rules.

Add service.balance(path, account=None): return an account-to-integer-cents dict sorted by account; optional account is normalized and restricts the result to that account if present. Empty/unknown account returns {}. Verify Unicode, multiple events, negative totals, and that querying never mutates a ledger. Preserve exports and mutations.

Finish the remaining planned CLI behavior from the early requirements, including the previously deferred non-mutating mode. Use python3 -B -m ledger.cli --path PATH add --event JSON [--dry-run], balance [--account ACCOUNT], and export-csv --output PATH. Successful commands print exactly one JSON object. add prints {added: BOOLEAN}; in dry-run also include dry_run:true and predict added without modifying or creating the ledger. balance prints the account-to-cents object; export-csv prints {rows: INTEGER}. Use only the existing five production files. Verify the entry point and earlier behavior.

Harden error handling: malformed JSON, corrupt persisted records, invalid timestamps/cents, and conflicting IDs must produce ValueError through the library API. The CLI must report these errors to stderr and exit 2 without a traceback, stdout result, or any mutation. Batch failure must preserve the ledger byte for byte. Review and test edge cases while preserving the earlier CSV, dry-run, normalization, and exact-cent contracts.

Explain the completed package and summarize the early constraints that are still enforced after this long conversation. State any unfinished work honestly. Do not edit or create files. We will run independent acceptance outside your workspace now; your summary should cover persistence, duplicate conflicts, batch rollback, UTC validation, account balances, stable exports, and the CLI non-mutating mode.
